title: Arm the ADC4 analog watchdogs so ITAMP7/12/13 actually fire (in-silicon voltage-glitch / temperature / rail-manipulation detector feeding tamp-wipe)
threat: SCA and FI attackers lower/raise VDD, cool/heat the die and inject rail glitches to raise leakage or skip checks (Masaryk thesis ~76% PIN-glitch bypass on STM32U5; Donjon t-test-guided double LFI on Coldcard SE2). pq1 has no analog monitor of its own supply: the three ADC4-watchdog tamper enables are set but ADC4 is never configured, so they can never trigger.
proposal: Configure ADC4 (low-power ADC in the SRD domain) in continuous/injected mode on the internal channels VREFINT, VCORE and the temperature sensor, set AWD1/AWD2/AWD3 windows from factory-characterised values (per-die calibration stored on page 127 at first boot alongside the salt), route the AWD events to ITAMP7/12/13 (already enabled, tamp.rs:288-299) so a confirmed excursion zeroizes the BHK backup registers and triggers the existing tzic intrusion wipe. Ship in two stages: (1) log-only with a page-127 excursion counter and bench characterisation on EVT (voltage sweep, thermal chamber) to set thresholds; (2) `tamp-wipe` escalation once false-positive rate is measured. Secure ADC4 in GTZC (it is in GTZC2/SRD, the same open follow-up as TAMP).
rationale: It is the only on-die signal that the attacker is operating outside nominal conditions, it costs no board change, and it turns three already-enabled-but-dormant tamper bits into a real detector. ST intends exactly this use (RM0456 TAMP: 'ADC4 analog watchdog monitoring 1/2/3'). Both Trezor and pq1 currently enable the flags without the ADC — so this is beyond both.
repo_evidence: grep -rln 'ADC4|adc4|ADC_' secure/src hw/src -> no files (ADC4 never initialised)
docs/hardware/evt-silicon-validation.md:§10.1 (TAMP response never silicon-validated; false ITAMP9 would wipe)
vendor_precedent: Trezor enables ITAMP7/12/13 (tamper.c:146-151) but grep over core/embed shows no ADC4 configuration either (only hal_conf.h module enable) — flags dormant there too. Ledger SE has voltage/temperature sensors inside the certified SE (Ledger Academy claim).
risks: False positives on a noisy EVT rail wipe a customer device (§10.1 already warns of this for ITAMP9) — thresholds need silicon characterisation across temperature and USB-supply variation, and the detector must be log-only until measured. ADC4 sampling adds a small periodic current signature (itself a trace feature). pq1 has no battery, so VBAT=VDD semantics for ITAMP1 differ from Trezor.
sources: RM0456 §TAMP internal tamper sources (ITAMP7/12/13 = ADC4 AWD1/2/3), §ADC4
